usage: Usually refers to a formal business agreement or written deal. In Hong Kong usage, 合同 is common in workplace and commercial contexts; it sounds a bit more general than very legal-heavy wording.
Often appears with verbs like 簽, 睇, 改, 續, and 終止. You can say someone signs or checks a 合同, and it is also natural when talking about employment, service, or sales agreements.
For beginners, 合同 is a safe, everyday noun for a contract. If you want to sound more legal or official, you may also hear 合約 in similar contexts.
Use it when talking about an agreement between people, companies, or organizations. It is not usually used for casual personal promises unless they are made official.
